newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian c.bank bill volume dips, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Croatian c.bank bill volume dips, rates steady.

text.p: Bill volume dipped to only 43 million kuna ($7.3 million) at Croatia's central bank auction on Wednesday from last week's 414 million as commercial banks ran short of money to invest, the bank said.
"Liquidity is rather thin, and banks placed some money into (Finance Ministry) T-bills yesterday," one official told Reuters.
The National Bank of Croatia sold 40 million kuna in 35-day bills at a steady rate of 7.50 percent.
The rate it paid for the remaining amount in 91-day bills was also unchanged at 9.0 percent.
To help the banking sector liquidity, it had bought back 35-day paper last Friday in a repo deal, which expires on February 17.

The total injected into the system was 32.8 million kuna at a yield of 7.50 percent, the bank said. It had also proposed to buy outstanding T-bills, but no banks offered them. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 5.922 Croatian Kuna)
